task_preferences.reason: Both make one clear request; candidate-1 repeats the request. Candidate-3 adds a useful subject, while candidate-2 retains a slightly fuller courtesy close; neither difference supports a universal winner.
All preserve the same supplied facts, citation and inferential boundary. Different sentence grouping alone does not justify a ranking.

All follow the required teaching sequence and correct arithmetic. Candidate-1 explicitly defines the symbols, which could help a novice, but no audience evidence supports an overall quality preference.
All accurately orient the listener and preserve the limit on inference. Candidate-3 adds an attention cue, but no delivery or audience evidence establishes that it works better.
Both document the exact command and supplied behavior without an unsupported execution-status assertion. Inline versus Usage formatting is a venue choice, not a basis for a quality rank.
Both retain that the scenario is constructed; candidate-1 omits that qualifier. The active versus passive retest wording does not justify a further preference.
The three outputs are identical to one another and to the supplied complete original.

limitations: One model judgment per candidate, no human review or inter-rater reliability estimate.
The reviewer knows the broad study design from the authorized protocol, but the method-to-label key remained unseen.
Constructed tasks have no genuine personal voice ground truth.

The execution-status and fixture-qualification failures are explicit interpretations of the supplied-facts-only rule; a human may disagree and should record that disagreement rather than overwrite this record.
No aggregate superiority, human-likeness, causal benefit or author-identity conclusion follows from these ratings.
